title: Deferred Fixed Annuities: Closing Interest Credit on a Full Surrender
content:
**Product:** Deferred Fixed Annuities — the Ashgrove Flexible Premium Deferred Annuity and the Ashgrove SecureRate 3, 5, 6, 7 and 10.

## Rule

When a full surrender is handled, the contract's interest is closed by crediting the part-year surrender interest, dated the day it is credited, to the contract value.

| Aspect | Effect of the credit |
|---|---|
| Entry | One interest credit entry on the contract, dated the day it is credited |
| Contract value | Raised by the part-year surrender interest |
| When it applies | Whenever a full surrender is being handled on the contract |

## Waiting state

The part-year surrender interest is worked out only after every excess partial withdrawal on the contract carries its surrender charge entry.

Put the other way: while any withdrawal that the activity history shows as an excess partial withdrawal has no surrender charge entry of its own, the part-year surrender interest is not yet worked out.

## Crediting tool: `credit_surrender_interest_88d8dad0`

**Capability.** Credits the part-year interest that closes a Deferred Fixed Annuities contract's interest for its surrender: it records, dated today, one interest credit entry on the contract and adds the interest to the contract's current contract value. Afterwards the activity history shows the new interest credit entry and the contract shows the raised contract value.

**How it is invoked.** It is an agent-side tool: unlock it with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool`, then call it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`, passing the tool name `credit_surrender_interest_88d8dad0` and its arguments.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `fixed_contract_id` | The reference number of the Deferred Fixed Annuities contract the interest is credited to, as read from the contract lookup | Identifier, as recorded |
| `interest_amount` | The interest credited, in US dollars; it is added to the contract value as given | A positive amount with exactly 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent before it is passed |

**Return.** A one-line confirmation: "Interest <entry reference> credited to contract <contract reference>: <amount>; contract value now <value>." The entry reference is the new interest entry's reference number; amount and value are US dollar amounts with 2 decimal places. Receiving this line means the interest entry exists and the contract value has been raised by the amount. No other return is defined.

*Illustration (hypothetical values):* `interest_amount` 652.97 on a contract valued at 100000.00 returns a line ending "contract value now 100652.97".
